setlist.title: Stuck In Mobile With The Memphis Blues Again

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Stir It Up** (2 reviews): Played only one verse, appearing unrehearsed, though the final chorus featured a nice three-part harmony; Singer clearly could not remember much beyond the chorus, making it a bustout rather than a slot [23][26]
- **Row Jimmy** (1 review): One of the finer periods for this song, where the show really shines [31]
- **Stuck Inside of Mobile With The Memphis Blues Again** (1 review): Videos from the show show the band having fun with this tune [30]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Bobbie's guitar performance in this song is described as a bit cheesy [31]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): Described as a spacey jammed treat in the second set [28]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-03-26.sbd.miller.91158.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 161 min; rated 4.38/5 by 8 [1]. Said about its sound: Nice overall quality with audience sound livening the recording without getting in the way [23]
- **gd1988-03-26.mtx.tobin.95488.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 161 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [3]. Said about its sound: Loud static burst in Mexicali Blues and three dropouts in The Wheel [3]
- **gd1988-03-26.mtx.dts.tobin.95931.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 161 min [6]. Said about its sound: Loud static burst in Mexicali Blues and problems in The Wheel [6]
- **gd1988-03-26.113740.SBD.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 161 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]

## Around the show

- Weir was loud and more out front in spring 1988 than in previous years [24]
- Jerry sounded pumped, with vocals as good as possible for him at that career stage [28]
- Raucous crowds rode the wave of high-energy sets during this renaissance period for the band [29]
- Considered as good as any representative example of the Spring 1988 run by an attendee [27]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-03-26.sbd.miller.91158.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK SA-X90) D [1]. Also: Two different SBD Cassette Masters were used to make the show complete [1]
- **gd1988-03-26.mtx.tobin.95488.flac16**: transferred by Kevin Tobin; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [3]. Also: Transfers and mastering by Charlie Miller, using TDK SA-X90 and Nakamichi DR-1 masters [3]
- **gd1988-03-26.mtx.dts.tobin.95931.flac16**: transferred by Kevin Tobin; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [6]
- **gd1988-03-26.113740.SBD.flac16**: source: SBD Analog Cass Master-> DAT-> CDR -> ? -> FLAC [2]

Nice overall quality with audience sound livening the recording without getting in the way
Weir was loud and more out front in spring 1988 than in previous years
Singer clearly could not remember much beyond the chorus, making it a bustout rather than a slot
Considered as good as any representative example of the Spring 1988 run by an attendee
Jerry sounded pumped, with vocals as good as possible for him at that career stage
Described as a spacey jammed treat in the second set
Raucous crowds rode the wave of high-energy sets during this renaissance period for the band

claims.song: Stuck Inside of Mobile With The Memphis Blues Again
claims.text: Videos from the show show the band having fun with this tune
One of the finer periods for this song, where the show really shines
Bobbie's guitar performance in this song is described as a bit cheesy
Two different SBD Cassette Masters were used to make the show complete
Transfers and mastering by Charlie Miller, using TDK SA-X90 and Nakamichi DR-1 masters
Loud static burst in Mexicali Blues and three dropouts in The Wheel
Loud static burst in Mexicali Blues and problems in The Wheel

facts.lineage: Dolby B was used on the Master Cassettes. The Master Cassettes were played back with Azimuth adjustment and Dolby B decoding on a Nakamichi CD1 into a Korg MR1000 at DSF 1 bit 5.6MHz. Subsequent conversion to 24/96 AIFF done via Korg Audiogate software. Redbook CDR standard 16/44.1 files were created using Bias Peak, Izotope Ozone's MBIT+ (for all dithering), and Weiss Saracon SRC (all sample rate conversions).
